sources.location: https://ftp.pride.ebi.ac.uk/pride/data/archive/2024/04/PXD031084/MQ_search_results_proteome.zip and MQ_search_results_phospho.zip (summary.txt, MQ_parameter_file/mqpar.xml, HTTP range reads)

claims.value: proteome: 38 RAW x 10 channels = 380 rows; phospho: 12 RAW x 10 channels = 120 rows
claims.evidence: 54 PRIDE files = 50 RAW + 2 MQ zips + FASTA + Experimental_design.docx; all RAW claimed

claims.location: comment[label], source name, factor value[disease], treatment
claims.value: TMT126..TMT131N -> animal pools A1+A6+A11.. (Sham/CTRL, ch 1-5) and B1+B6+B11.. (TAC/HF, ch 6-10)
claims.evidence: Experimental_design.docx table (Animal No., Group, TMT channel, TMT label); paper: 3 sinus nodes pooled, 5 pools per group, TAC=HF group, sham=CTRL
MaxQuant summary.txt Raw file -> Fraction column (both zips)

claims.location: organism, strain, sex, developmental stage, sampling time
claims.value: Mus musculus; C57BL/6N; male; adult; 8 week
claims.evidence: Methods: 8-week-old male C57BL/6N mice; sinus node isolated 8 weeks post-surgery. 'adult' is inferred from age (8 weeks at surgery, ~16 weeks at sampling)
Methods 2.1: transverse aortic constriction (HF group) or sham (CTRL group); PRIDE disease DOID:6000 congestive heart failure applies to the TAC arm only
paper 'sinus node'; PRIDE BTO sinus node; UBERON:0002351 sinoatrial node chosen as the matching term
Both RAW headers: Method of Q Exactive HF-X; Q Exactive HF-X - Orbitrap MS; paper MS2 at 60,000 resolution in Orbitrap

claims.location: dissociation method, collision energy, acquisition method
claims.evidence: RAW method XML Fragmentation_HCD normalized 32, 'nce: 32'; paper: data-dependent Top10, HCD, NCE 32. Both checked RAW files agree
Two-step Lys-C then trypsin digest in paper/PRIDE; MaxQuant enzyme Trypsin/P. Column is single-valued so Trypsin chosen per record naming; Lys-C not encodable

claims.value: Carbamidomethyl C fixed; TMT6plex K and any N-term fixed; Oxidation M and Acetyl protein N-term variable; phospho only: Phospho STY variable
claims.evidence: mqpar.xml of each zip via sdrf-tools search-params (TMT10plex isobaric labels mapped to TMT6plex UNIMOD:737; MaxQuant treats them as label not fixed mod)
mqpar mainSearchTol 4.5 ppm; FTMS MatchTolerance 20 ppm (Orbitrap MS2)
Sample processing protocol: 5 mM TCEP, 10 mM CAA
Protocol: micro-flow reverse-phase UPLC off-line fractionation (78 concatenated to 38; phospho 12). pH not stated so high-pH term not used
Each channel is a pool of 3 mice (A1+A6+A11 etc.). Replicate integers 1-5 are placeholders numbering the pools within each group (per source-name), not a deposited numbering

limitations: Lys-C step of the digest cannot be encoded: comment[cleavage agent details] is single-valued; reconcile flags cleavage_agent_incomplete (missing Lys-C) and this is accepted. MaxQuant searched Trypsin/P
Phospho and proteome share the same TMT10-plex pool; the two SDRFs are separate sub-experiments of the same 10 samples

Phospho enrichment chemistry (e.g. TiO2/Fe-NTA/IMAC) was not found in the PRIDE protocol or the paper Methods text searched (Europe PMC full text; supplementary file not read), so characteristics[enrichment process] is omitted
developmental stage 'adult' is inferred from the age statement; exact age at sampling not stated
organism part: sinoatrial node chosen as ontology match for the paper's 'sinus node'
biological replicate integers 1-5 are placeholders for the pooled channels; not stated numbering
treatment values 'sham operation' and 'transverse aortic constriction' are not found in the NCIT/EFO cache (validator warnings); kept as stated in the paper; C57BL/6N free text warning from validator
validator error 'study sample not found in pride' is the known cache artifact (term PRIDE:0001013 valid live); value kept
Acquisition dates not annotated; only method-file timestamps (2019-12-17, 2019-12-23) were seen in the two RAW headers read; other RAW files not read, though file names indicate the same two batches
comment[sample preparation batch], tissue mass, age at sampling not available in the record
